$comment: HABLO machine manifest: what `install.mjs` puts in place. Edit here, not in the script.

defaults.$comment: What a bare `./install.sh` assumes. --profile / --ladder on the command line win; AWS_PROFILE in the environment wins over defaults.profile.

pi.$comment: settings are applied only where the key is absent (never overriding a value you set); enabledModels is only extended when an allowlist already exists (creating one would hide every non-bedrouter provider).

fallbacks.$comment: When the probe says a rung is not entitled on this account, try these Bedrock IDs in order before dropping the rung.

cli.$comment: The `hablo` command: start a firstmate captain from any project directory (bin/hablo, stamped with the firstmate dir) plus the Pi extension that injects firstmate's AGENTS.md. User-space only: no sudo, no /usr/local.
cli.$comment2: model: what `hablo` passes as --model when you pass none; null = the chosen ladder's auto alias (auto / auto-oss). --cli-model overrides.

firstmate.$comment: kunchenguid/firstmate is an agent distro, not a Pi package: a git clone whose AGENTS.md takes over the harness you launch inside it. The installer sets config/crew-harness to pi and writes crew-dispatch.json so every crewmate is `pi --model bedrouter/<auto>` explicitly.
firstmate.$comment3: baseBranch: the integration branch ticket branches are cut from and merged back into (--base-branch overrides). The policy never targets the repository's default branch directly.

tools.$comment: What firstmate's bootstrap reports as MISSING when absent; installed by step 11 exactly as firstmate's own `install:` hints say. npm ones go to npm's global prefix; the two scripts install into ~/.local/bin (treehouse picks it because it exists and is on PATH; no-mistakes via NO_MISTAKES_LINK_DIR), so no sudo. `setup hooks` (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode session hooks) is deliberately not run: Pi does not use them and they write outside ~/.pi.

firstmate.$comment2: backend: null keeps firstmate's auto-detection (tmux). Set "herdr" (or pass --backend herdr) to write config/backend.

backup.$comment: What `backup` archives and `--restore` puts back. essentials: state that cannot be regenerated and is not in dotfiles. history (only with --with-history): sessions, caches, logs.
backup.$comment2: config: normally regenerated by dotfiles or this installer; archived anyway (cheap) and restored only where missing.
